content.thinking:
I need to write the whole file carefully in one pass without testing first. For the dwarf, I'm designing a stocky ~1.3m figure, and since he's holding a blunderbuss, I'll angle the arms forward and slightly outward as a compromise between a neutral rest pose and a gun-holding stance.

Now I'm working out the skeleton coordinates: hips at mid-height, a spine chain rising to chest, neck, and an oversized head with a helmet reaching toward the 1.3m total height. For the legs, I'm placing hip, knee, and ankle joints with slightly bent reach lengths so they fit the proportions, planning to add foot and toe joints off the ankle tip, and settling on a side convention for mirroring left/right limbs across the body.

I'm positioning the shoulders and working out the gun's pose — grip, foregrip, stock, and muzzle placed diagonally forward and slightly upward with a flared barrel end — then starting to lay out the arm joints from shoulder to elbow to wrist to match the gun-holding stance.

I'm checking distances between shoulders and hand targets against reasonable arm segment lengths, adjusting hand positions on the grip and foregrip so the chunky dwarf proportions can actually reach without exceeding arm span, then figuring out elbow bend directions to keep the pose natural.

Now I'm laying out the gun geometry itself, defining the stock-to-muzzle axis and positioning the stock so its butt rests plausibly against the character's chest.

I'll create a "gun" joint parented to the chest since the hands move with the arms while the gun stays static in rest pose. For the gun geometry, I'm planning a tapered wooden stock, brass butt plate, steel lock plate with hammer, torus trigger guard, and a swept barrel that widens from breech to a bell-shaped muzzle, with brass bands and a darker lathed interior for the bell.

Working out the lathe profile for the barrel and bell shape...

Checking the inner wall stays within the outer wall near y=0.52, that looks fine. I'll keep the lathe smoothing at 0 with 12 segments and a steel paint color, orienting along the z-axis, and simplify the gun by keeping its axis purely horizontal rather than computing a tilt direction.

Now I'm working out hand placement on the gun: positioning the right hand at the grip and the left hand on the foregrip wrapping the barrel, then checking reach distances from each shoulder to make sure the arm lengths can actually span the gap, adjusting the foregrip position slightly closer to bring it within reach.

I'm also checking for overlap between the gun's stock and the chest geometry, since the torso's depth at shoulder height might intersect with the stock near the wrist area, so I may need to shift the gun forward slightly while keeping the grip reachable.

The beard also needs adjustment since its braids could overlap with the gun in the reference image—the beard sits above the gun with its tip just grazing the top of the barrel, so I'll set the beard length and gun height so they overlap only slightly, with the gun placed in front (greater z-depth) of the beard.

Now I'm working out the gun's placement and proportions: stock from z=0.2 to 0.55 with the grip hand at 0.33, and a barrel roughly 0.6 meters long to approximate a blunderbuss scaled down. I'm defining the lathe profile for the barrel in meters, setting up outer radius points along its length to shape the bell-mouth end.

Still adjusting outline points...

I check that the inner wall points stay thin enough relative to outer at each z-height, tweaking one inner point from 0.052 to 0.048 to avoid an overly thin wall near the bell flare, and confirm the outline order avoids self-crossing. I'm also placing the left hand at the foregrip under the barrel around z=0.45.

Now I'm working out the arm geometry for the left hand gripping the foregrip, checking shoulder-to-hand distance against possible arm segment lengths and adjusting the shoulder position and hand target to keep the reach plausible for a stocky dwarf build.

For the right hand on the grip, I'm computing the distance from shoulder to hand target and finding it fits with a slight outward elbow bend.

Then I'm moving to the torso, building a spine chain from hips through spine, chest, to neck base using a series of loft points, and checking how the chain names map to the path points for the rigging.

Settling on names ["spine1","spine2","chest"] for the spine chain, then setting up a body sweep using loft with the hips and spine as the bone stations.

Working out the station widths and heights along the torso path, tapering from hips to belly to chest to shoulders.

For coloring, I'm planning a hand-painted look: a leather vest over blue sleeves with gold trim, using a gradient based on surface normal to fake top-lit highlights and bottom shadows, plus some noise mottling for texture rather than flat toon shading.

Still writing shading logic...

Checking texel density across roughly 5m² of paint confirms resolution is plenty at 1024, so I'll bump paint size to 2048 for crisper detail. I'm staying mindful of the 64 flat-colour cap by relying mostly on paints (which aren't counted) and reserving flat colors for small accents, now starting to lay out the palette with skin and hair tones.

Now I'm extending the palette with navy blue, gold trim, leather browns, steel grays, cream fur, and wood tones, then sketching the body-part breakdown starting with legs—pants, boots, and chain detailing for the dwarf's lower half.

Still tuning leg sweep radii and boot color bands...

For the cuff, I'm adding a fur ring lathed around the boot top using a small outline shape, positioned along the shin axis near the knee. Since the limb is mostly vertical, I'll simplify by using a vertical lathe axis positioned at the right height rather than computing the exact bone direction.

Now I'm working on the feet: positioning the ankle, then building the boot sole as a flattened box, sweeping a capsule shape from ankle to toe for the boot body, and adding a small steel toe cap sphere at the front.

I'm attaching the toe cap to the toe joint, then building the leg limb from hip to ankle with knee bend, chaining hip, knee, and ankle bones together using the point array as the path, with a sharp corner at the knee.

Now I'm placing the hip joints symmetrically and setting up the torso loft using the hips-to-spine bone list, then working out how to paint the torso: a blue tunic base with a brown leather chest harness layered on top, considering a front vest region for the paint pattern.

For the torso coloring, I'm going with a dark brown leather vest textured with a diamond quilting pattern, computed by mapping position onto two diagonal axes and drawing lines where the fractional values land near zero. I'm also adding a flared tunic skirt below the belt using a lathe shape from the hips down.

I'll just skip the scale hack and set skirt radii to cover the hip width and belly depth instead. Then I'm adding a front tabard panel extruded from a pentagon-ish outline in brown cloth with a gold diamond decal, plus planning a side tab piece next.

For finishing touches, I'll sweep a closed circular path around the skirt hem for a gold trim ring, and add an elliptical belt sweep at the waist using the same circle-point helper with slightly different radii.

I'm realizing there's a cleaner approach: using the surface's loop function to trace a path around the built mesh at a given height, which handles the geometry automatically instead of me guessing radii. I'll apply this for the belt with a slight lift, and consider reusing it for collar trims too.

Now I'm working out the skirt hem and neck/head rigging — using loop on the skirt surface for the hem, and setting up a short neck chain connecting the shoulders to the head joint, making sure to pull the correct parent joint from the spine chain's tip.

For the head itself, I'm placing it at a model-space center point and sizing the skull as a scaled sphere, aiming for the broad, large-featured look typical of a dwarf face.

The jaw gets its own joint and shape separate from the skull since it'll be mostly hidden by a beard and moustache anyway, so I'm using a flattened sphere for it positioned lower and forward, with the mouth essentially just a dark line underneath the facial hair.

Now I'm defining the nose as a bulbous sphere with a bridge sweeping up to the brow, adding tiny dark nostril spheres, and starting on cheek geometry.

Placing ruddy cheek spheres, then working out a heavy angled brow ridge made of capsules per side, colored like the red hair and tilted downward toward the nose for an angry look, before starting on the small white eye spheres set beneath it.

For the eyes I'm layering sclera, iris, and pupil spheres with warm cream, pale blue, and dark tones, positioned under the brow for shading, and then adding small pointed ears mostly hidden beneath hair or helmet cheek guards.

Nose placement protrudes nicely to 0.259. Now I'm designing the helmet as a blue dome with gold bands, lathing a profile that sits above the brow line and covers the skull's top, sizing its radius to roughly match the skull curvature.

I'm checking clearance between the helmet rim and the brow capsule — the rim sits close to the brow front, so I'm considering lifting the helmet slightly higher so it doesn't collide with the brows.

Now I'm positioning the gold rim band as a closed ring around the helmet's base, then adding a second crest strap that sweeps from front to back over the dome.

Still computing dome geometry...

Now I'm designing the cheek guards as gold-trimmed blue pentagon plates on either side, with a slightly larger gold base extruded behind a smaller blue front plate for the rim effect.

For the back of the helmet, I'm adding a red ponytail as a capsule shape sweeping down and back. Then I'm working on the signature beard—a large red braided mass that sweeps from the chin down over the chest, defining a path of points from the jaw area downward across the torso to build the loft shape.

Defining beard taper widths...

I'm wrapping that in a `lit()` helper to add shading highlights based on surface normal and facing direction. Then I'm planning the braids hanging from the beard sides, like gold-ringed plaits with three tail strands, built from chains of flattened diamond shapes angled alternately to mimic a plaited look, keeping part counts low by using around 8 segments per braid.

Writing braid geometry...

Writing diamond pattern paint function...

Then moving to the mustache geometry: planning a huge handlebar mustache with two curling sweeps built from catmull-rom curves starting under the nose.

Adding sideburn and hair details connecting to the beard loft stations.

For the braids, I'm skipping a back ponytail and instead placing three beard braids: two side braids near x=±0.095 descending from y1.03 to y.8 with slight forward z-offset, tapering tails with gold rings around y.9, positioned to sit in front of the main beard mass without clipping through it.

Checking against the gun's position, I notice the braids overlap the gun stock's z-range, so I'm shortening the braids to end around y0.88 and lowering the gun's axis to y0.78, raising the stock slightly so its top clears under the braid tails -- keeping both elements visually separated.

Next I'm placing the hands around the gun: right hand gripping the trigger area and left hand cupping under the barrel's fore-stock, which I'm defining as a wooden box beneath the round barrel to give the grip a believable shape.

I'm checking the arm reach distances against the shoulder and hand-grip positions, and the arms are coming out nearly fully extended rather than bent like the reference pose. I'm considering either lengthening the arm segments or pulling the gun's grip point closer to shorten the reach.

I'm now placing the gun's butt against the chest and working out the stock length to grip-to-lock distances, then recalculating where each hand should land on the gun to keep the arms bent naturally.

I'm also figuring out elbow bend hints so the limbs curve outward and down correctly for each arm, then setting up the arm chain naming convention (shoulder, elbow, wrist, hand) per side.

Now I'm planning the arm's visual layers: sleeve geometry sweeping along the chain with tapering radius, plus a leather bracer on the forearm and a glove at the wrist, with fur cuff trim near the elbow.

I'm orienting the lathe outline along the actual arm direction (shoulder-to-elbow vector) rather than a fixed vertical axis, defining the fur cuff shape and placement, and sketching out the shoulder pauldron as a scaled blue sphere with gold trim.

Adding a gold rim band and a ring of small stud spheres around the pauldron dome, figuring out placement so the studs sit at the right height on the curved surface.

Now I'm thinking through draping leather straps over the torso, like suspenders running from each shoulder down to the belt, defining rough path points along the chest for a surface sweep.

I'll add a gold buckle at the middle and a row of gold rivets along each strap, plus a cream wool fur ruff collar sweeping as a closed loop around the neck base to match the reference's fur ruff detail.

For texture, I want to scatter small cream fur tuft cards across the collar and cuffs—around 120 cards using a single tuft texture tinted cream, scattered on the surface of the ruff sweep with minimum distance spacing to avoid clumping. Now I'm moving on to elaborate the weapon details.

Setting up the gun's central axis along y=.78, then shaping the stock as an extruded profile from the butt at z=.19 to the wrist at z=.34, working out the classic blunderbyss-style outline coordinates in the z-y plane with the thickness running along the x-axis.

I'm placing the right hand center near the grip area and checking its reach distance from the right shoulder joint, which comes out around 0.40, acceptable. Then I position the left hand under the forestock, wrapping it slightly below and verifying that reach distance too, roughly 0.47, which also seems fine.

Now I'm shaping the stock geometry with a thickness of 0.05 and a bevel for the wood grain, setting up a local coordinate frame along the gun's axis so I can define the forestock profile, barrel start position, and breech location in these u/v terms.

Settling on the barrel: start it at z=0.30 with length 0.64, ending at z=0.94, and I'm sketching the radius profile along its length with a muzzle flare up to radius 0.09 near the end, double-checking the inner/outer radius consistency at a few key points to make sure nothing clips through the surrounding wood.

Now I'm figuring out gold decorative bands for the barrel, estimating the local radius at a few positions along it and sizing small ring outlines so they wrap snugly around the barrel's varying thickness, including a wider rim near the mouth.

Still shaping the muzzle ring geometry...

I'm distinguishing inner versus outer flare surfaces by their normal direction so I can darken the interior and keep the exterior steel-colored, then considering adding a gold engraved knot decal near the top of the bell.

Placing decals on the bell's curved surface, deciding on three positions (top and both sides) with projection direction matching each face.

Now I'm working out the flintlock mechanism: a steel lock plate on the stock's right side, a curved hammer sweep built from spline points with jaws, and starting on the trigger guard as a quarter-torus arc beneath the stock.

Still working out the trigger guard curve and spike geometry...

Now I'm adding gold details: a butt plate box at the stock rear, and gold side plates with an engraved knot texture facing outward on each side of the stock.

I'm also adding a thin steel ramrod positioned under the barrel, tucked beneath the forend between the barrel underside and the stock bottom, then moving on to plan a powder horn and pouch for the hip gear.

For hip accessories, I'm placing a leather pouch with a flap on the right hip and a small wooden keg with gold hoops lying sideways on the left hip, checking that the keg's position doesn't collide with the bent elbow of the arm resting nearby.

I considered adding a bandolier with gold charge-tube vials across the chest, but decided to skip it since the beard, gun, and existing suspenders already crowd that area. Now I'm thinking through knee guards -- blue plate armor with gold rims positioned on the front of each knee, which requires computing the knee joint location from the limb geometry first.

Building knee plate geometry...

For the boots I'm adding leather strap details with small gold buckles, wrapping circular loops around the shin at three different heights using a sweep technique.

Now I'm adding gold rivet studs as individual small sphere parts scattered across the armor, keeping the total part count manageable around 350. For the skirt hem, I'm designing a paint pattern that applies a gold Greek-key style band with a dark zigzag motif near the bottom edge, switching from the base blue color when the height falls below a threshold.

I'm also figuring out the tabard panel placement, calculating the skirt's radius at different heights along its lathe profile so the front panel sits flush against the curved surface at the correct depth and vertical position.

I'll also decal a gold buckle onto the torso, and plan similar gold ring trim decals for the shoulders. For textures, I'm sketching an SVG knot-plate design for gun armor plates, and separately a leather panel texture with a brown background, gold border, and blue inner accent.

Writing more SVG texture code...

Now I'm working through hand geometry: palm boxes with finger capsule rows, figuring out orientation so the right hand grips the gun from the correct side with fingers wrapping around properly.

For the left hand I'm mirroring the structure: palm positioned on the outer (shoulder) side of the forend with fingers wrapping toward the far side, roughly symmetric to the right hand's setup but flipped in x.

Now I'm tallying up the joint hierarchy: hips, spine, neck, head, jaw, legs with toes, arms, plus the gun, landing around 22 joints total, and considering whether to add finger or beard-braid joints for extra detail but leaning toward skipping them for now.

I'm sketching back-of-body details since the reference doesn't show that angle: a small leather backpack with straps and a bedroll cylinder on top, plus a cream fur mantle draped over the shoulders, while skipping a cloak for simplicity.

I'm adding a fur collar ring and fur cuffs to match the reference's visible fur peeking beneath pauldrons and at the collar, then double-checking the triangle budget stays reasonable.

Now I'm setting up the module imports needed for the helper functions, making sure only the utilities I'll actually use (frame, lerp, rng, offset, path and paint helpers) are included to avoid unused-import type errors.

I'm defining the metadata export with the asset name, description, and Blizzard-style commit tag, then setting up light and shadow color constants and a shading function that computes rim highlights and shadow falloff based on surface normals.

Finishing the lit() function with speckled noise blended into highlight or shadow colors, then noting I need to import the Paint type for the return signature.

Now I'm defining material paints for wood grain along the z-axis, blue woven cloth, mottled leather, and a mottled fur texture...

For steel I want mottled gray tones with scratch-like grain, gold as a flat high-contrast highlight color, and skin as a warm mottled tone. I realize I need to import the mottle function alongside the others.

For the vest, I'm computing diagonal seam lines using absolute-value modulo math so the pattern wraps cleanly, then blending between leather brown and dark tones depending on whether a pixel falls near a seam, wrapping the whole thing in the lighting function so nested paints resolve correctly. I also need to handle that the torso is split between a blue tunic and brown vest, so I'll lerp between them based on position.

I decide to make the torso mostly leather vest with quilting on front and back, keep sleeves blue, and give the pauldron blue too, rather than overcomplicate with face-normal blending.

Now I'm setting up the skeleton builder, defining the hips joint as root with a spine role, then building a catmull-rom spine chain from hips through spine1, spine2, to chest using three control points.

Next I'm lofting the torso surface between the hips and spine bones to form the vest shape, then extracting a surface from that sweep, and building a hex-sided belt loop sweep around the torso at the waist height.

Neck connects torso to head with a sweep from y.95 up to the head at y1.05, colored skin tone and hidden partly by the beard. Checking shoulder placement: torso width at y.9 is .5, so shoulder joints sit at x±.25, right at the surface edge where arms should attach, parented to the chest.

Writing arm chain logic... computing shoulder-to-hand positions per side with naming convention S="L" or "R" based on sign, building limb points with bend directions, and chaining them as arm joints with shoulder/elbow/hand names parented to the chest.

For the sweep I'm tapering the arm radius from shoulder to wrist with decreasing values, then banding sleeve, bracer, and glove regions along the forearm's parametric length, placing the glove near the fist and planning gold-rimmed bracer plates.

Now I'm thinking through how to cut perpendicular loops across the forearm surface using the chain's tangent frames rather than a fixed-up direction, since the arm sits roughly horizontal. I'll place gold bracer bands at specific points along the sweep with riveted detailing, and consider whether to skip the lathed fur cuff in favor of a swept version instead.

Working out the fur cuff as a sweep around a loop with a bit of outward lift, plus a gold shoulder trim band tucked under the pauldron. For the pauldron itself I'm positioning it at the shoulder using an outward-up axis, sizing the lathe dome so its base radius and height properly cover the upper arm joint where it meets the sleeve.

Now I'm attaching the pauldron to the shoulder joint of the arm chain, then adding a gold rim trim as a second lathe ring with a simple non-intersecting outline. For the emblem on top, I'm placing a small gold octahedron scaled flat into a diamond plate shape.

Adding a pyramid-shaped stud on top using a 4-sided cone, positioned so its base sits just above the pauldron dome with the apex rising slightly higher. Then I'm decorating the pauldron with a ring of small gold spheres arranged symmetrically around it using a frame-based ring helper.

I'm working out that items placed via literal frame positions default to the nearest bone, but I can pass an explicit bone to override that, and I'm confirming the ring geometry forms a circle perpendicular to the given axis direction. I still need to compute the normalized axis vector for positioning the lathe shape correctly.

Now I'm setting up the leg loop: computing hip and ankle positions symmetrically for each side, building the limb chain with knee bend based on the distance and segment lengths, then naming the joints hip/knee/ankle with the leg role and foot contact points. I'm starting to sweep the pants geometry over the thigh chain next.

Still defining boot radii...

Reference boots have fur at the top, so I'll use the fur color for the cuff to match that calf detail. Now I'm adding boot straps along the sweep, creating a ring strap near the ankle with a slight lift and small radius.

For the gold buckles at the front, I need to figure out the correct orientation on the boot's surface -- since the boot sweep runs downward, angle 0 corresponds to the front-facing side. I'll place small gold box buckles seated along the surface normal at the strap positions.

Now I'm moving to the knee plates and the foot joint structure, planning the sole as a box positioned at the ankle, sized with the heel offset back and the appropriate width and length for the foot shape.

I'll keep the toe as a smooth sphere and add a separate toe bone joint parented to the ankle, with the toecap riding on it and the sole/foot sweep staying attached to the ankle bone. For details I'm adding sole rivets, a darker welt and heel box coloring, a gold rivet on the steel toecap, and checking that boot width fits within the foot spacing at x=±.14.

Now I'm moving to the head/jaw rig: building a neck chain from chest with a two-point path, sweeping it with a skin-colored radius, then attaching a head joint and a jaw joint off the neck's last point with appropriate aim directions. I'm also placing a skull part as a scaled sphere on the head bone.

Adding jaw, cheeks, sideburn hair, and ear parts...

Now planning the beard: single rigid bone to head, lofted strands using catmull path stations wrapping around the jaw and chin, starting near the chin and widening at stations like (0,1.10,0.14) with roughly .26 width.

I'm checking that the beard depth stays clear of the chest front and gun stock geometry, then setting up a grain-textured material for the strand coloring.

Now I'm thinking about adding beard lock detail — five curved sweeps draping from the chin down the beard surface using lighter hair color for texture variation.

I'm also starting to write a braid function that chains spheres along a catmull-rom path running down each side of the head...

Still writing braid geometry...

Adding gold engraved rings...

Still writing engraving paint logic...

Still writing mustache sweep geometry... checking the mustache and nose positioning relative to the mouth, and confirming the mouth stays hidden behind the beard before moving on to eye placement.

Now I'm defining helmet pieces: a lathed dome bone-linked to the head, painted blue with highlights, plus a gold rim band created via a closed ring-point helper swept into a circular path, with a thinner secondary band being added next.

Adding helmet bands and crest arches...

Testing a superellipse-style exponent (2.6) instead of a pure ellipse to better match the outline shape, checking it against the actual radius values at a few heights to confirm it fits better. I'm working out a parametric dome function using this exponent for both the horizontal and vertical components.

Still refining the outline points...

Working through the plate geometry, I check that the diamond plate center and thickness keep it within the dome surface bounds. For the cheek guards, I'm placing them as extruded plates hanging from the rim sides down to the jaw area, positioning them just outside the skull radius using x-coordinates scaled from the dome geometry.

Still computing plate offsets...

Now I'm adding hair as a tapered braid curve with decreasing radius toward the tip, then sketching backpack details: a leather box shape plus a bedroll cylinder strapped across the top.

I'm positioning gold buckles on the straps and figuring out a belt buckle decal placed on the belt surface using a small textured plane facing forward.

Now I'm working out the skirt tabard geometry via lathe, checking outline points against the belt and thigh radii to make sure the skirt clears the hips and thighs properly.

Writing hem paint logic...

I'm also planning a front tabard decal panel on the skirt, positioned and sized to project onto the curved surface near the front at roughly z=.25.

Now I'm checking clearances for the gun and keg accessories against the skirt and elbow position, placing the keg at the left hip with a cylinder rotated so its axis runs along z, strapped horizontally against the hip.

Still writing keg details...

Now adding a right hip pouch with a flap and gold buckle, plus a curved powder horn hanging behind it with a bone color and gold cap, built from a swept capsule shape.

Skipping any chest brooch since the reference only shows strap details there, keeping the gold buckle where the suspenders meet instead. For the fur ruff, I'm sweeping a neckline curve and scattering fur card textures across its surface with orientation following the surface normals, then applying a similar scatter technique to the arm cuffs.

I'm designing a fur tuft SVG with three tapered tufted lock shapes in cream and tan tones for the texture atlas, alongside panel, buckle, knot plate, and bell rune textures. For the gun, I'm adding engraved gold barrel bands via a lathe operation and a steel lock plate, while skipping the rear sight detail.

Now I'm setting up a gun joint attached to the chest bone for positioning the weapon, and planning finger and fist geometry for both hands -- working out palm box dimensions and mirrored x-offsets so the right and left hands grip symmetrically.

Checking the left hand's reach distance - it comes out near .50 which is close to full extension, so I should pull the z-coordinate in slightly to .41 to allow a bit more bend at the elbow.

Now adjusting the right arm to bend more strongly, then moving to the hands - placing capsule shapes for the four fingers, a palm box, and a sphere for the rounded knuckle area.

Still shaping the glove...

I'm setting up the thumb as a capsule angled forward from the palm, then noting the hand bone should attach to the arm's tip joint, and defining the glove leather color. Now I'm moving on to laying out the gun's component coordinates starting with the stock extrusion.

Defining the stock outline...

I'm checking that the outline points don't self-intersect and verifying the bottom edge is monotonic, then working through how the barrel's cylindrical radius relates to the stock's cross-section so the barrel sits mostly enclosed within the stock profile.

Now I'm positioning the lock plate against the stock side and confirming its thickness doesn't clash badly with the barrel, then placing the left hand near the forend before adding the butt plate as a thin box at the rear face of the stock.

Next I need to handle the trigger guard and trigger, then the barrel with its bands, rim, and decals, and finally the lock plate with hammer and pan — deciding which side to put the lock on given the ambiguous three-quarter camera angle, so I'll place it on both sides to be safe.

I'm checking for geometry collisions: the lock plate position may overlap with the right-hand fingers wrapping the grip, so I'm nudging the lock forward along z to clear the fingers, and double-checking the left hand's palm position for similar overlap.

Checking that fingers and palm positions don't collide with the lock plate — adjacent z-ranges seem fine with slight overlap at the top. Reach distance for the left arm comes out close to .53-.54, nearly fully extended, so I'm considering lengthening the arm or adjusting shoulder position to make the geometry work on a 1.3m frame.

Now I'm positioning the flintlock mechanism itself: the steel lock plate, hammer (with a curved sweep toward the pan), frizzen, and pan boxes, all offset slightly in x to clear the barrel radius, plus small gold screw spheres on the plate and gold side plate textures on the stock.

Positioning gold side plates...

Deciding against extra glow or embellishments to keep budget reasonable, settling on a tabard, pouch, keg, backpack, and bedroll for the character's gear, then starting to write the coordinate helper function.

Writing imports...

Defining more paint presets...

Defining more material colors...

I'll simplify VEST to a paint function returning seam color versus base leather color directly, skip the extra lit wrap since leather's already lit. The torso uses this vest paint, with gold studs placed along the strap rows, and sleeves just use the blue cloth color. Now I'm starting to define the panel texture as an SVG.

Writing SVG code...

Writing more decorative SVG elements...

Figuring out the decal placement parameters — positioning the barrel text on top and sides using the right direction and up vectors, and sizing the drawing area to fit the bell's curved surface.

I'll drop the top decal and just use two side decals instead, positioning them near the surface tangent points along the lathe's z-axis so they align with the body's radius at that height. Now I'm ready to write out the full code covering fur ruff, torso, head, and arm loops, along with the chain point helper for positioning.

Setting up the builder and skeleton...

Finishing the torso loft stations, I realize the rounded cap at the top station will extend past the final point by its radius, pushing the silhouette higher than intended.

Flattening the top plane at the neck gives sloping shoulders naturally as the torso narrows. I'm building out the surface definitions for torso, belt loop, neck sweep, and skirt lathe, adding paint colors and a gold rope hem, plus belt studs along the loop.

Writing stud placement logic...

Writing arm chain and sleeve geometry...

Adding gold bracer bands with studs, then moving to the hand geometry and checking the arm's joint structure, three joints for shoulder, elbow, and hand tip. Planning similar loop treatment for legs and boot straps.

Now I'm working through the chest pack details, a box with a flap lid and a bedroll cylinder, but checking for collisions with the ponytail and helmet. I'm adjusting the pack's vertical position lower on the back to avoid overlapping the hair geometry.

I'm placing the gold buckles and vertical straps on the pack's back face to attach the bedroll convincingly.

I'll skip bands on the bedroll lathe and instead use torus straps with a cylinder for the blanket roll in a red-brown color, and skip adding a tin cup or pick to keep part count manageable. Now I'm ready to write the full code, making sure part geometry calls and point/frame inputs are typed correctly.

I'm setting up small helper functions for sphere and box geometries, then planning the final file with a keg, pouch, horn, pauldron ring frame, scatter randomization, and various utility functions for color mixing, noise, and smoothing already established. Writing braid function...

Adding braid tip spike...

Now I'm lathing engraved rings at two points along the path, checking that the lathe outline stays non-negative on x and comparing ring radius against the braid sphere width.

Checking ring sizes at both t positions confirms they fit relative to the braid thickness, adjusting outer radius slightly for the first ring. I'm reusing the hair material for eyebrows too, and now adding a nose bridge capsule connecting two points to give the nose more structure.

Next I'm setting up the beard using a draped sweep surface with alternating hair colors for a lit, highlighted lock effect, plus curled mustache tips. The loft and sweep setups for the beard and knee plate look structurally sound with proper bone references and tolerances.

Now I'm positioning the knee plate shields—gold outer and blue inner extrusions—calculating the correct z-offset so they sit just forward of the bending knee joint, accounting for the leg's radius and the rounded corner where thigh meets shin.

I'm defining the outline points for the outer and inner shield shapes as small diamond-like polygons, scaling the inner one down to about 72% so it nests inside the outer plate. I also need to make sure these outline arrays are typed correctly as tuple arrays rather than generic number arrays to avoid a type error.
